thread.title: Mark Carney to Be Sworn In as Prime Minister on Friday
thread.title_full: Mark Carney to Be Sworn In as Prime Minister on Friday

author: Omid Ghoreishi
title: Mark Carney to Be Sworn In as Prime Minister on Friday
text:
Mark Carney will be sworn in as Canada’s next prime minister on March 14.
In a statement in the evening of March 12, the office of Gov. General Mary Simon said she will be presiding over the swearing-in ceremony at the Rideau Hall at 11 a.m. on March 14.
Carney won the leadership race of the governing Liberal Party with a wide margin on March 9. His win with 85.9 percent of the nearly 152,000 votes cast put her ahead of former Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Finance Chrystia Freeland with 8.0 percent of the votes, followed by former cabinet minister Karina Gould with 3.2 percent and former Liberal MP Frank Baylis with 3.0 percent.
Carney, a former central banker, has already been meeting with Trudeau and cabinet ministers as part of the transition.
Carney will become a rare prime minister who currently isn’t a sitting parliamentarian, and will be the first Canadian prime minister who has never held an elected role before.
The former governor of Bank of Canada hasn’t yet declared how he intends to get a seat in the House of Commons, and whether he‘ll seek it via a byelection or he’ll call an election soon.
The Parliament was prorogued by Prime Minister Justin Trudeau on Jan. 6, on the same day he announced he is planning to resign, and started a leadership race to replace him.
The Parliament is set to return on March 24.
Opposition parties have indicated they intend to vote non-confidence in the government. However, most recently, the NDP said it won’t vote for bringing down the government until the House votes to pass an aid package for Canadians impacted by U.S. tariffs.
An election needs to be held by October this year.
